title: Unified signal fusion for SLO forecasting and graded alert routing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: Our SLO engine currently treats traces, metrics, and logs as siloed signals. This results in noisy paging (false positives on transient spikes), slow anomaly attribution, and brittle burn-rate calculations during multi-region rollouts. Scope: build a lightweight "signal fusion" layer in the observability pipeline that ingests trace-derived latency distributions, aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99), and error-rate counters, normalizes them, and feeds a unified timeseries into the SLO/burn-rate engine. Deliverables: 1) tracing hook changes to emit latency histogram deltas and sampled spans with minimal overhead; 2) a transformation stage in the metrics pipeline that synthesizes a fused signal (weighted combination + smoothing + seasonality adjustment); 3) a graded alerting policy that maps fused-signal confidence to paging tiers (silent, on-call DM, pager); 4) anomaly-detection thresholds using rolling baselines and change-point detection for attribution; 5) dashboard and runbook for oncall and incident responders. Non-goals: replacing full APM or implementing a long-term ML forecasting stack in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks emit histogram-delta events for 99th/95th/50th latency buckets under 2% added p99 latency overhead on high-throughput routes
Metrics pipeline produces a fused-signal timeseries for at least three production routes (chat-gen, embeddings, rerank) available in Grafana
Burn-rate engine can ingest fused signal and generate graded alert levels with configurable thresholds per service
Paging policy implemented: silent alert -> DM escalation -> pager based on confidence and sustained burn-rate over 3 minutes
Automated anomaly detector catches injected regression in staging (PR with synthetic spike) and creates a labeled incident in the test Slack channel
Docs updated: runbook, configuration examples, migration checklist for teams that want to opt-in
